analytic.title: Analyzing Real-time Schedulability of Resource-oriented Distributed Real-time Embedded Software

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: As computer systems become increasingly internetworked, Distributed Real-time Embedded (DRE ) software is becoming increasingly common and important, a challenging problem faced by researchers and developers of DRE software is how to devise and implement a method that can effectively analyze requirements in varying operational conditions. In this paper, a Distributed Real-time Embedded net (DREN) is proposed as software design specification modeling tool. The basic tasks, function module and communication process are modeled by using DREN, thus forming the entire application by making use of Petri net's synthesis operation. Time Reachability Graph is adopted to analyze the correctness of DREN model, the basic properties of DRE system are also considered. Finally, a specific example is given to simulate the analytical process, the results show that the method can be a good solution to analyze DRE software.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: With the development of computer technologies, Distributed Real-time and Embedded (DRE ) software is becoming increasingly common and important as the underlying technology for distributed computing and networking systems [1]. DRE software is often characterized by complexity and volatility of requirements, developers require tools that support the rapid evaluation of design models against systemlevel temporal and functional properties. Basically, in a DRE system, if timing constraints are not met, the consequences can be disastrous, including the great damage of resources or even loss of human lives. For example, a brake-by-wire system in a car failing to react within a given time interval can result in a fatal accident [2].

To address these challenges, we extend for Place Timed Petri net and propose a Hierarchical Distributed Real-time Embedded net (DREN ) model. The tasks and the relationship between task of DRE software is modeled in detail. In particular, we abstract communication process as a task, and using DREN model to describe resource and time delay of communication process, thus forming the whole application. Based on the constructed model, Time Reachability Graph Corresponding author:Yunxiang Liu , Email address: yxliu@sit.edu.cn is adopted to analyze the correctness of (DREN) model, the basic properties of DRE software are also considered, thereby reducing the complexity of analysis.

The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 presents the computation model. Section 3 model DRE systems. Section 4 proposes the analysis technologies for DRE software. In section 5, a specific example is given. Section 6 presents some related works while section 7 is conclusions.

div.head: A. Requirements of DRE software
div.p: Because DRE software generally has a strong performance requirements, such as predictability, efficiency, reliability and security, et al. Therefore, it is necessary to fully consider the above characteristics when describe the requirements of DRE software.

Definition 6: The requirement model of DRE software is a 7-tuple Ψ = (T K, NT, RS, RL, CP, RT, D):T K is a finite tasks set; N = {N 1 , N 2 , . . . , N n } is the collection of tasks set, the jth task in module N i is denoted by T K i,j ;RS is a finite resources set;RL is the relationship between task, which may be sequence, choice, parallel et al;CP : T K → (N * × N * × N * ) is the property function of task, which describes the running time and priority of task.RT : T K → RS * is the resources function of task, whose function is to assign the necessary resources to each tasks, RS * represents the multiple sets of resource, that is, a task can use multiple source;D is the deadline of whole application.

div.head: B. Schedulability Analysis
div.p: For the bounded DREN, because its reachability state set R(S 0 ) is a finite set, therefore, R(S 0 ) is viewed as a vertex set, and the direct reachability relationship between state is viewed as arc set, and the transition is marked in the corresponding arc, which constructs a directed arc. The directed graph is called Timed Reachable Graph in DREN model.

Let Ω be a DREN model, S is a state of Ω, if ∃p i,j dm ∈ P , which makes M (p i,j dm )=1, then S is called the overtime state of Ω; if ∃t i,j d ∈ F T (S), then S is called the dangerous state; if M (P e )=1, then S is called the normal termination state of Ω, denoted by S F .

The model is schedulable if all module can complete before their deadlines, which is called a feasible schedule. From the view of DREN, the feasible schedule corresponds to the transition firing sequence from initial marking S 0 to normal termination state. Mapping into the state space is: Ω is scheduling iff S F is schedule in Ω. With the number of transition and place increasing, the scale of time reachability graph will greatly increase. To this end, we propose a heuristic search algorithm to computing the feasible scheduling.

The algorithm only uses part of the necessary time reachability graph to compute the feasible scheduling. As the path is generated from part of time reachability graph, therefore, it may not be optimal. The algorithm view the initial state as root node, and gradually compute each state of feasible scheduling, then doing the following operations for current state S: Step 1: Marking S (whose function is to avoid computing the computed path, thus reducing the workload of computation), then going to Step 2; Step 2: If S is the normal termination state, then outputting the feasible schedule, otherwise go to Step 3; Step 3: Computing firing set F T (S) of S, if F T (S) = ∅, then outputting the error info, otherwise go to Step 4; Step 4: Judging whether all sub nodes of S have been marked, if it is, then stepping back and updating the feasible schedule; Step 5: Computing the next unmarked node of current node by combining with the greatest concurrent set, if the new state may fire the overtime handling operation of a task, then re-calculating the next unmarked node of current node, otherwise going to Step6; Step 6: Updating the feasible scheduling, and setting current state as new state, then going to Step 1.

div.head: V. EXPERIMENTS
div.p: In order to better describe the above modeling process and explain the correctness of analysis process, we use Electronic Toll Collection (ETC ) as an example. ETC system is an advanced system which consists of high-tech equipment and software such as microwave technology, electronics technology, computer technology, communications and network technology, and can achieve the function of automatically charging the cost of road without stopping vehicle.

The workfolw of ETC is: the system will display traffic light after starting, and inform lane computer of sending startup instructions to antenna controller when trigger coil detects the passage of vehicles. The read information from OBE will be sent to data processing center for data processing and charging. If success, then charge information screen will display 'charge successfully, the amount of consumption'; the system mainly adopt camera and capture on the spot, and throguh traffic police department to do the corresponding handling. The general distance of charging is 30m. The design speed of ETC lanes is 40km/h, and the handling time of whole applications is 0.09s. Supposing each processor has 20 memory , communications cache is 2, bus tokens is 1. the requirements of preemptive and deadline are given in table II, the mainly considered resource including: memory, communications cache, bus tokens, in which time unit TTU is 2ms, and resource unit is Mb. principle of CAN bus is also met. And we can draw that the model is scheduling.

div.head: VI. RELATED WORKS
div.p: In recent year, there has been some related works used for DRE systems design including the non-formal methods and formal methods. The followings are related non-formal methods: In [5], the authors proposed a global framework to support Distributed Real-time and Embedded application development based on methods, such as pattern, component middleware and model-driven. And analyzed quality of service of Distributed Real-time and Embedded systems (energy, faulttolerate, scheduling etc). P.Paul et al [6] used task graph to describe tasks and relations between tasks in DRE systems. More specifically, it discussed the schedulability analysis of DRE systems, and introduced several design optimization problems characteristic of this class of systems.

Although the non-formal methods has made some corresponding results in the design of DRE systems, but they may cause some of the semantic ambiguity, in order to solve this problem, there has been some formal methods: G. Madl et al [7] used Time Automata (TA) to model various components of the non-preemptive real-time distributed embedded systems and converted the system scheduling problem into TA state reachability. As the TA model implied the existence of global clock, it unfits for modeling the Distributed Systems. V.Marcel et al [8] used the time extended of Vienna Development Method (VDM++) to stipulate DRE systems, and used VDM verification tools to verify the properties of system. A resource-based time Petri Net is proposed in [9] to model the DRE systems and analyzed the corresponding semantic, properties. But it didn't describe the communication between modules which is the key issue of DRE systems.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, we have proposed an DREN to model and analyze DRE software. This approach is based on a formal model, Petri net, that allows to consider different components of DRE software. The main contributions of this paper are: (1) we proposed an DREN model to better describe describe DRE software, thus providing effective management to DRE software; (2) summarizing the modeling process of DRE software in detail, such as task, resource and communication process; (3) analyzing the correctness of constructed model and related properties of DRE software, thus ensuring the correctness of designment.

The study of DRE software is still underway at present. Our current research is focused on exploring formal method as means to improve its mapping into DRE 's architecture. The following two aspects are the main work in the next phase:
(1) further improves this method, consider the fault-tolerant of each task to assurance system's schedulability; (2) developing the corresponding tools to support the modeling.
